query: For rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys intended for magnetic refrigeration, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields while maintaining rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability? State one controlled intervention that would test the hypothesis, the observations predicted relative to a baseline, the boundaries over which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence that would support it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys (HEAs) that undergo a first-order magneto-structural transition near room temperature, refining the grains into the 20–100 nm range while introducing a very high density of coherent twin boundaries (<20 nm spacing) lowers the interfacial energy barrier for forward and reverse transformation. This lets a larger volume fraction transform under low magnetic fields, boosting the magnetic-entropy change, while the twin interfaces provide reversible nucleation sites that cut hysteresis and simultaneously strengthen the lattice and shorten thermal heat-flow paths.
generation.material_initial_state: Solution-annealed, coarse-grained (≈20 µm) equiatomic Fe–Co–Ni–Mn–Al high-entropy alloy showing a B2-rich/FCC dual phase, a magneto-structural transition at ≈300 K, |ΔS_M|≈4 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 2 T, ~5 K thermal hysteresis, thermal conductivity κ≈10 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ and compressive yield strength ≈850 MPa.
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to high-pressure torsion (≈6 GPa, 5 turns, room-temperature) to produce a fully nanocrystalline (20–100 nm) microstructure containing >10¹⁴ m⁻² coherent twin boundaries.
generation.conditions: Characterise both the baseline and SPD-processed states between 250 K and 340 K in magnetic fields up to 2 T; thermal and mechanical tests at 300 K in air.
generation.structural_mediator: High-density grain/twin boundaries produced by severe plastic deformation.
generation.mechanism: Twin and grain boundaries act as low-energy nucleation pathways, reducing magnetoelastic strain energy during the first-order transition. The easier, more reversible interfacial motion enables a larger transformed fraction at small fields (higher |ΔS_M|) and suppresses internal friction (lower hysteresis). The dense interface network blocks dislocations (raising strength) yet shortens thermal diffusion lengths (retaining or improving κ).
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the coarse-grained baseline, the nanocrystalline-twin-rich alloy will show: (1) ≥30 % larger peak |ΔS_M| at 2 T, (2) ≥50 % reduction in thermal hysteresis width, (3) ≥20 % higher room-temperature thermal conductivity, and (4) ≥20 % higher compressive yield strength.
generation.baseline: Identical alloy in the coarse-grained, solution-annealed state tested under the same magnetic, thermal, and mechanical protocols.
generation.boundary: Expected to hold for Fe/Co/Ni/Mn/Al-containing HEAs (valence-electron concentration 7.5–8.5) that exhibit a first-order magneto-structural transition within 250–340 K and can be grain-refined without amorphisation. Effect may vanish for grain sizes <10 nm (transition suppressed) or >500 nm (insufficient interface density).
generation.uncertainty: The exact change in thermal conductivity is uncertain; excessive defect scattering after severe deformation could counteract the anticipated κ increase. Very fine grains might also broaden rather than sharpen the transition.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a single 50 g ingot of FeCoNiMnAl HEA, section it into two halves. Keep one half as coarse-grained baseline after solution anneal (1100 °C/2 h, water quench). Process the second half by high-pressure torsion at 6 GPa for five turns. Measure: (i) isothermal M(H) curves every 2 K near 300 K up to 2 T; calculate |ΔS_M(T)|; (ii) M(T) on heating/cooling at 0.01 T to extract hysteresis width; (iii) thermal diffusivity (laser-flash) and density/heat capacity to obtain κ; (iv) quasi-static compression to 20 % strain for σ_y.
measurements: Compressive yield strength σ_y at 300 K
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SPD-processed sample shows (a) ≤10 % increase in |ΔS_M|, or (b) ≤10 % reduction in ΔT_hyst, or (c) ≥10 % decrease in κ, or (d) ≥10 % decrease in σ_y, versus the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
